findings.title: verifySafeHtml throws raw RuntimeException, crashing the build instead of reporting a message
findings.body: When the derived English reference file cannot be opened (see separate finding), or the current file cannot be re-read, verifySafeHtml throws a plain RuntimeException. The surrounding verify() method only catches IOException and wraps it into a MojoExecutionException; an uncaught RuntimeException will propagate out of the mojo and abort the build with a stack trace rather than being added to the reported `messages` list. A verification tool should report the problem as a message (or wrap it in MojoExecutionException) so users get a readable diagnostic.

findings.title: English-file path rewriting is wrong for community-only theme directories, causing the verifier to fail
findings.body: The English reference file is computed as file.getAbsolutePath().replaceAll("resources-community", "resources").replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties"). This only works for files under themes/src/main/resources-community whose English counterpart exists under themes/src/main/resources. For the JS themes (js/apps/admin-ui/maven-resources-community and js/apps/account-ui/maven-resources-community) there is no sibling "maven-resources" directory containing the _en file in the community repository, so the English bundle cannot be loaded and the verifier throws a RuntimeException (see other finding) for every such file. Additionally, many community-only locales (e.g. messages_ca, messages_ka under resources-community) have no _en-independent counterpart issue but product resources may lack them too; any locale file whose English file does not exist at the rewritten path will crash the verification rather than being skipped or reported.

findings.title: Java MessageFormat choice syntax is not supported by the account UI's JS i18n stack
findings.body: error-invalid-multivalued-size was changed from 'Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).' to 'Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.'. The keycloak.v3 account theme is a React app whose message properties use double-brace interpolation ({{0}}, {{1}} everywhere else in this file). The single-brace Java MessageFormat/ChoiceFormat syntax is not evaluated by that JS i18n stack, so users of the account console will likely see the literal string '{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}' (and possibly un-interpolated {0}/{1}/{2}) instead of a pluralized message. The same change is made in js/apps/admin-ui/maven-resources-community/theme/keycloak.v2/admin/messages/messages_en.properties (error-invalid-multivalued-size) which is also a React (i18next) UI. The choice format is correct only for the server-side FreeMarker themes (themes/src/main/resources...), where those files were updated consistently.

findings.title: Italian text introduced into Lithuanian message files
findings.body: totpStep1 in the Lithuanian account messages was replaced with 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:' — an Italian sentence. The same Italian text was also put into themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/login/messages/messages_lt.properties (loginTotpStep1, line 71). Lithuanian users will see Italian on the OTP setup page. It should be translated to Lithuanian (e.g. 'Įdiekite vieną iš šių programėlių į savo mobilųjį telefoną:').

findings.title: PropertyResourceBundle reads the file as ISO-8859-1 while the duplicate-key check uses UTF-8
findings.body: verifyNoDuplicateKeys reads the file via Files.readString (UTF-8), but verifySafeHtml loads the same file with new PropertyResourceBundle(new FileInputStream(file)), and PropertyResourceBundle(Properties.load(InputStream)) decodes as ISO-8859-1. These message files are UTF-8 (Arabic, Chinese, Thai, etc.), so the values used for HTML comparison will be mojibake. In most cases value and sanitized are corrupted identically so the comparison still passes, but any character whose UTF-8 bytes contain 0x3C ('<') or 0x26 ('&') in a trailing byte after ISO-8859-1 decoding can produce spurious 'Illegal HTML' findings or, worse, hide real differences. The bundle should be loaded with an InputStreamReader specifying UTF-8.

findings.title: containsHtml only recognizes lowercase tags, so uppercase HTML in the English source disables HTML in translations
findings.body:
HTML_TAGS = Pattern.compile("<[a-z]+[^>]*>") only matches lowercase tag names. If an English source string contained e.g. '
' or '

' (case-insensitive HTML is legal), containsHtml() returns false and POLICY_NO_HTML is used, while the OWASP sanitizer strips tags case-insensitively — a translation carrying the same uppercase tag would be flagged, and one with lowercase variants would be inconsistently treated. Use (?i) in the pattern.
